PAPERS.title: Premature mortality and economic losses attributable to landscape fire-related PM2.5 in ten countries and territories: a causal analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Population-weighted daily landscape-fire PM2.5 vs non-fire PM2.5, 2-day moving average, modelled
PAPERS.n: 1,366 communities in ten countries and territories, 47,844,851 deaths, 2000-19. Each 1 ug/m3 rise in 2-day mean landscape-fire PM2.5 raised mortality 0.60% (95% CI 0.19-1.00) and mortality-related economic losses 0.59% (0.21-0.97); 906,869 deaths and US$994.5 billion attributable (AF 1.90% and 1.64%). The headline number is the disproportion: fire PM2.5 is 19.0% of ambient mass but 30.6% of PM2.5-attributable deaths. Instrumental-variable estimates exceeded conventional association estimates by a median 56.0% (2.2-111.3), i.e. classical designs are biased toward the null here. The instrument is the weak point - it is not named in the abstract, and IV validity (exclusion restriction against co-emitted gases, weather confounding) carries the whole causal claim. Value-of-statistical-life transfer across ten economies adds its own uncertainty, not propagated into the CIs. For sensing: mass-only monitoring cannot separate the fire fraction, so the 4-fold potency gap this implies is invisible to a network that reports total PM2.5.

PAPERS.title: Distribution-sensitive assessment of air-quality and health benefits from clean-heating pilots in northern China.
PAPERS.pm: City-daily PM2.5 from 1-km gridded product, ML weather-normalised, heating-season mean/P95/P99
PAPERS.n: 88 clean-heating pilot cities, 2013-23. The distributional result is the point: the policy cut the heating-season mean only 3.01 ug/m3 but P95 by 5.76, P99 by 5.96 and exceedance days by 7.92 per season - the tail moved twice as far as the mean, which a mean-only evaluation would have missed entirely. HIA gave 12,454 fewer attributable all-cause deaths (95% CI 8,564-16,222), 88.9% from the 2017-18 rollout cohorts and 56.2% from the top decile of cities; high-pollution days were 27.8% of improvement days but 48.8% of the mortality difference. Benefit is therefore concentrated in both time and space. Weaknesses: ASCM counterfactuals rest on donor-pool comparability in a decade of nationwide declines, and the mortality figure is a transfer from an exposure-response function, not an observed death count. Argues directly for dense networks resolved enough to capture episode tails rather than annual means.

PAPERS.title: Exposure-response relationship between ambient PM2.5 and SO2 with COPD and small airway dysfunction prevalence among individuals at high risk for COPD in Yunnan Province, China: a threshold analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient annual PM2.5 and SO2, residential assignment
PAPERS.n: 11,095 residents aged 20+, multistage random cluster sampling, 2021-22, with spirometry in questionnaire-screened high-risk individuals. COPD prevalence 27.2%, small airway dysfunction 53.6%. Restricted cubic splines gave significant nonlinearity for both pollutants and thresholds of 21.33 ug/m3 PM2.5 and 8.67 ug/m3 SO2; above the PM2.5 threshold COPD and SAD prevalence were 33.4% and 58.4%. Random-forest importance ranked air pollution above smoking and biomass fuel, which is a strong claim from a cross-sectional design and should be read as variable importance, not effect size. The real limits: no temporality, exposure assigned without residential history, and the enriched high-risk sampling frame means these prevalences do not transfer to a general population. A 21 ug/m3 threshold is well above the WHO 5 ug/m3 guideline and close to the regional mean, so it is plausibly a data-support artefact rather than a biological inflection.

PAPERS.title: An umbrella review of public health interventions to mitigate air pollution and improve health outcomes in high-income countries.
PAPERS.pm: Intervention-level exposure change (traffic policy, portable air cleaners, net-zero pathways)
PAPERS.n: Eight systematic reviews covering city and transport policy, household exposure reduction and emission-reduction modelling. Transport interventions gave consistent cardiovascular benefit and fewer traffic injuries; portable air cleaners cut indoor PM2.5 with modest blood-pressure improvement; modelling studies projected a median ~1.5% mortality reduction under large-scale mitigation. The ordering matters - structural policy beat individual and household measures, which were complementary rather than substitutive. Two weaknesses limit its use. Equity was rarely assessed and inconsistent where it was, so the review cannot say who benefits. And the 1.5% figure comes from models, not measured outcomes, which mixes evidence tiers inside a single summary. Only eight reviews, all high-income, so nothing here transfers to the settings where PM2.5 burden is largest.

PAPERS.title: Toxic Air Contaminant Emissions from Residential and Commercial Fossil Gas Appliances: A Systematic Review.
PAPERS.pm: Appliance emission factors for 41 toxic air contaminants, leakage and combustion pathways
PAPERS.n: 25 studies, first systematic synthesis of emission factors across gas appliance types. Nonzero emissions documented for at least 41 toxic air contaminants via both leakage and combustion. Only formaldehyde and benzene had enough data for quantitative characterisation, and their emission factors spanned two orders of magnitude across studies and operating conditions - a spread that makes any single-value inventory estimate indefensible. Coverage is badly skewed to cooking stoves; heaters, water heaters and dryers are barely studied despite longer duty cycles. The authors' suggestion that methane and CO can proxy for leakage- and combustion-related TAC emissions is the operationally interesting claim and is stated as emerging rather than established. For indoor sensing this is the calibration target: cheap CO and CH4 channels as inference surrogates for species no low-cost node can measure directly.

PAPERS.title: Greenspace, air pollution and respiratory health outcomes: a systematic review of cohort studies.
PAPERS.pm: Residential greenspace (NDVI and similar) with co-assigned ambient air pollution
PAPERS.n: 14 cohort studies to May 2026, all rated good on the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, predominantly European. Greenspace was generally protective against air-pollution-associated respiratory mortality, and the methodological finding is the useful one: effects appeared more consistently through mediation than moderation, implying greenspace acts by improving local air quality rather than by raising individual resilience. That distinction has direct design consequences - if the pathway is mediation, greenspace and PM2.5 must not be entered as independent covariates in the same model without care. No pooled estimate is reported, so the synthesis is narrative and effect magnitude is unavailable. Greenspace and pollution are both strongly confounded by socioeconomic position, and near-complete European coverage limits transfer. Relevant to siting: greenspace gradients are a known source of within-city PM2.5 heterogeneity.

PAPERS.title: Associations between household solid fuel use, kitchen ventilation, and depressive symptoms among older adults in China: a national cross-sectional study.
PAPERS.pm: Self-reported household fuel type and kitchen ventilation, no measured concentration
PAPERS.n: 11,697 CLHLS participants aged 65+, 2018 wave. Depressive symptoms (CES-D-10) in 26.87%; solid fuel use in 29.67%. Solid fuel carried OR 1.25 (95% CI 1.09-1.44) for depressive symptoms against clean fuel, and B = 0.57 (0.33-0.82) on the continuous score - a consistent but small shift, roughly a fifth of a scale point per unit. The charcoal subgroup showed a larger estimate on n = 39 exposed and the authors correctly flag it as unreliable. No interaction between fuel type and kitchen ventilation, which undercuts the paper's own framing that ventilation modifies the exposure. Exposure is entirely self-reported category, with no PM2.5 measurement, so the dose is unknown and misclassification is certain to be substantial. Cross-sectional design cannot exclude reverse causation, since depressed older adults may differ in household energy choice and reporting.

PAPERS.title: Biomonitoring of urban ultrafine particle exposure and associated health effects.
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine particle counts in exhaled breath condensate, industrial vs control urban setting
PAPERS.n: 99 hospital staff - 50 in the industrial Haifa Bay area, 49 Tel Aviv controls - with spirometry, FeNO, exhaled breath condensate and saliva at baseline and one year. Latent class analysis found a cluster with higher BMI, raised EBC ultrafine particle concentration and elevated salivary LDH-calcium, predominantly Haifa residents, reporting more cough, sputum and atopic complaints. The idea is worth watching: EBC particle burden as an internal-dose biomarker would close the gap between a fixed monitor and what a person actually inhaled. The execution does not support the claim yet. n = 99 with LCA on a handful of variables will find clusters whether or not they are real; no ambient UFP measurements are reported alongside the biomarker, so external-to-internal dose is never tested; and BMI loading on the same cluster makes an exposure interpretation hard to separate from a metabolic one. Occupational setting, not general urban.

PAPERS.title: The Silent Intruders: Cardiovascular and Pregnancy-Related Health Effects of Ultrafine Particulate Matter.
PAPERS.pm: Ultrafine particulate matter, number-based rather than mass-based metrics
PAPERS.n: Mechanistic synthesis of experimental, controlled-exposure and epidemiological evidence linking ultrafine PM to cardiovascular injury, with an emphasis on hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Pathways covered: pulmonary and systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, autonomic imbalance, endothelial injury and disturbed angiogenic balance, extended to maternal cardiovascular adaptation and placental vascular development. The review's honest core is its attribution problem - it states plainly that UFPM-specific findings are hard to separate from PM2.5, diesel exhaust particles, engineered nanoparticles and traffic-related pollution generally, and that direct developmental evidence is largely animal. Uncertainties named: particle translocation, exposure metric, critical gestational windows. No pooled estimates. The exposure-metric point is the operational one: UFP is a number-concentration phenomenon and mass-based networks, including nearly all low-cost optical nodes, do not measure it.

PAPERS.title: Combined PM2.5 and microplastics exposure exacerbates allergic asthma via OPA1/SLC7A11-mediated airway epithelial ferroptosis.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and microplastic co-exposure, ovalbumin-sensitised murine model and MRE cells
PAPERS.n: OVA-induced murine asthma plus OVA-stimulated MRE cells exposed to PM2.5 and/or microplastics. Co-exposure amplified inflammatory infiltration, goblet-cell proportion and lung-function impairment beyond either agent alone, with raised ROS and MDA and reduced T-AOC, CAT and SOD. Ferroptosis markers moved coherently: Fe2+ accumulation, lipid peroxidation, NCOA4/FTH1/ACSL4 up, SLC7A11/GPX4/GCLC/GSS down, alongside mitochondrial depolarisation, ATP depletion and reduced respiratory complex activity. OPA1 knockdown and ferrostatin-1 both attenuated the injury, which is the strongest part of the design - two independent interventions converging on the same pathway. What it cannot support: no dose-response is reported against realistic ambient concentrations, and instillation or high-dose culture exposures routinely exceed inhaled doses by orders of magnitude. PM2.5 composition is unspecified, so 'PM2.5' here is one sample, not a class.

PAPERS.title: Inhibition of condensable particulate matter by co-firing biomass and high sulfur coal on a 50 kW self-sustaining combustion furnace.
PAPERS.pm: Condensable particulate matter mass and speciation, mg/MJ, dilution sampling
PAPERS.n: 50 kW one-dimensional self-sustaining furnace, high-sulfur coal co-fired with corn stover or pine wood at 10% and 20% blend. Baseline condensable PM was 6.72 mg/MJ, 83.3% inorganic. Co-firing cut it to 5.09 and 3.85 mg/MJ (corn stover 10%, 20%) and 5.36 and 4.55 (pine wood), so corn stover at 20% removed 43% - the stronger effect traced to suppression of sulfate-associated inorganics and organic precursors. PAHs and sulfur-containing organics fell below detection at 20% blending. Relevant because condensable PM is invisible to hot-filter methods and to every optical low-cost sensor, yet it can rival filterable PM in mass; source inventories built on filterable-only sampling are biased low. Limits: a single bench furnace, one coal and two biomass feedstocks, no ageing or atmospheric processing, and condensable PM measurement is notoriously method-dependent, so absolute values should not be compared across sampling protocols.

PAPERS.title: A multi-angle and polarization-based retrieval algorithm for aerosol layer height of smoke and dust.
PAPERS.pm: Aerosol layer height from HARP2/PACE multi-angle polarimetry, validated against EarthCARE ATLID lidar
PAPERS.n: Optimal-estimation retrieval that adds multi-angle polarimetric information to conventional spectral aerosol-layer-height methods, exploiting polarisation sensitivity to the Rayleigh-versus-aerosol scattering contrast. Information-content analysis shows the added dimensions raise the degrees of freedom for signal relative to radiance-only observations - a quantified rather than asserted gain. Applied to HARP2 on PACE and validated against ATLID on EarthCARE, RMSE was 1.03 km over all collocated samples. That is the number to hold onto: roughly a kilometre of vertical uncertainty is still coarse against a 1-2 km boundary layer, so this constrains plume altitude rather than resolving surface coupling. Validation is against a single spaceborne lidar with limited collocation statistics and no ground-truth profile network. For surface PM estimation this is the missing variable in AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion: column loading aloft versus in the mixed layer is the dominant error term, and smoke and dust are exactly the cases where it bites.

PAPERS.title: An AI-based algorithm for retrieving aerosol optical depth and single scattering albedo using All-Sky Imager observations.
PAPERS.pm: AOD and single scattering albedo retrieved from all-sky camera imagery, sun-photometer targets
PAPERS.n: Machine-learning retrieval trained on co-located sun-photometer AOD and SSA at two sites, Beijing_PKU in East China and SGP in the central US. Independent validation gave r > 0.86 for AOD at all wavelengths with RMSE below 0.25, and for SSA r = 0.74 (Beijing_PKU) and 0.84 (SGP) with RMSE below 0.09. SSA from a consumer-grade sky camera is the striking result - absorption is normally the hardest aerosol property to retrieve and demands a calibrated multi-channel photometer. The obvious caveat is the one the authors state: two sites, so the model has seen two aerosol regimes and two instrument configurations, and the AOD RMSE of 0.25 is large where ambient AOD is low. As a low-cost densification path this sits alongside optical PM nodes - an imager and an ML model substituting for a photometer is the same economics that drove PurpleAir, with the same transferability question yet to be answered.

PAPERS.title: Advanced insights into biomass burning aerosols during the 2023 Canadian wildfires from dual-site Raman and fluorescence lidar observations.
PAPERS.pm: Multi-wavelength Raman, depolarisation and fluorescence lidar profiles of transported smoke
PAPERS.n: Dual-site observations of transported smoke from the 2023 Canadian wildfires, May to September, at ATOLL (France, Raman lidar with a 466 nm fluorescence channel) and GPI (Russia, five-channel broadband fluorescence excited at 355 nm). Upper-troposphere/lower-stratosphere layers showed higher depolarisation, slightly lower lidar ratios, lower Angstrom exponents and a redshifted fluorescence peak relative to free-troposphere layers; fluorescence magnitude and spectral shape agreed across the two sites and two instrument designs, which is the strongest evidence yet that fluorescence lidar signatures are transferable rather than instrument-specific. The consequential finding is negative: near-absence of hygroscopic growth at 90-100% RH contradicts the standard assumption that aged biomass-burning aerosol is hygroscopic. If that generalises, humidity-correction schemes for optical PM sensors - all of which assume kappa-Kohler growth - are systematically wrong during smoke episodes. One fire season, two sites, correlations with altitude at r2 0.61-0.68 that the authors concede is a proxy for injection height and plume origin.

PAPERS.title: A Theoretical Model for Predicting Visibility During Dust Events.
PAPERS.pm: Horizontal visibility derived from saltation-controlled dust emission and near-surface concentration
PAPERS.n: Physically based chain linking surface wind erosion to dust emission, near-surface concentration and visibility, with an analytical concentration-visibility relation closed heuristically and a moment-balance entrainment model that carries median particle size and soil cohesion into the threshold friction velocity. Against three published observational datasets the relation explained R2 = 0.62 of combined variability and had the highest R2 of the formulations compared under identical calibration. The appeal is that visibility is measured almost everywhere dust matters and PM10 usually is not, so a defensible physical inversion converts an existing observation network into a concentration proxy. R2 = 0.62 is not accurate enough for exposure assignment, only for event detection and screening. The authors are explicit that only the concentration-visibility link was evaluated - the emission and entrainment stages remain untested, and the full chain needs synchronised surface, entrainment, emission and visibility observations that do not exist.

PAPERS.title: A novel deep learning prediction method for PM2.5 integrating improved MSTL decomposition and FATA optimization algorithm.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 time series with meteorological and pollutant covariates, station-based
PAPERS.n: FATA-GSPMSTL-CNN-LSTM forecasting pipeline: RFECV plus Pearson screening for features, a grid-searched power-spectral variant of Multiple Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess for series decomposition, the Fata Morgana metaheuristic for hyperparameter search, and a CNN-LSTM head. Evaluated separately for heating and non-heating seasons in Guangzhou and Xianyang, and the seasonal split is the sensible part - these two cities differ in both source mix and meteorology. Beyond that the paper is a familiar pattern: four stacked components, no ablation isolating which one carries the gain, and improvement reported only against baselines the authors selected. No prediction intervals, so the forecast is a point estimate with no stated uncertainty - unusable for threshold-triggered alerting. Two cities and no external-city test means transferability is unaddressed. Metaheuristic hyperparameter search of this kind rarely survives comparison with a well-tuned gradient-boosted baseline.

PAPERS.title: Epidemiologic research on environmental chemical exposures and ovarian and endometrial cancers: a systematic review.
PAPERS.pm: Long-term ambient PM2.5, per 5 ug/m3, alongside other environmental chemical exposures
PAPERS.n: 145 studies screened, 54% ovarian-cancer only, 53% North American, 40% cohort; outdoor air pollution was the single most studied exposure class (27 studies, 18%). The pooled PM2.5 result is a clean null for ovarian cancer - HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.91-1.13) per 5 ug/m3 across four studies, and 0.94 (0.81-1.09) restricted to the three with co-pollutant adjustment. Endometrial cancer was weakly positive and implausibly precise: 1.02 (0.99-1.05) overall but 1.01 (1.00-1.01) with co-pollutant adjustment and 1.01 (1.01-1.02) for incident cases only. A confidence interval that narrow from five studies signals near-zero between-study heterogeneity or shared cohorts rather than genuine precision, and the authors do not report I2. Worth recording as a negative: gynaecologic cancer is one endpoint where the PM2.5 signal does not appear, against a literature that increasingly reports positive associations everywhere it looks.

PAPERS.title: Differences in the Effectiveness of Smoke Evacuator Types for Reducing Surgical Smoke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
PAPERS.pm: Optical particle counts at 0.3, 0.5, 1.0 and 5.0 um plus acetaldehyde and formaldehyde, 10-min sampling
PAPERS.n: Randomised, double-blind trial (UMIN000047033), 64 laparotomy patients at the University of Tokyo Hospital, Feb 2022 to May 2023, allocated 1:1:1 to electrocautery-incorporated evacuation at 8 mm tip distance (n = 22), 18 mm (n = 23), or hose-type (n = 21). The 8 mm system cut particle counts 96-97% across 0.3-5.0 um against hose-type; the 18 mm arm did not reach significance on particles, so effectiveness collapses over a 10 mm change in capture distance - the practically important result. Median acetaldehyde was 1.90, 2.70 and 7.90 ug/m3 in the 8 mm, 18 mm and hose arms, with both electrocautery arms below hose, and formaldehyde behaved similarly. Endpoints are area concentrations, not personal breathing-zone exposure, and no health outcome was measured. Single centre, n = 64, one surgical procedure type. The distance sensitivity is the transferable lesson for any point-source capture or near-field sensing geometry.

PAPERS.title: Heavy metal exposure and source profiling based on leaf-deposited particulate matter in Pune city.
PAPERS.pm: Leaf-deposited dust, ten elements, enrichment factors and PCA source profiles
PAPERS.n: 27 roadside, industrial, peri-urban, highway and rural sites in Pune. Elemental order was Ca > K > Fe > Na > Mg > Mn > Zn > Cu > Cr > Pb, consistent with crustal material, construction and resuspended road dust; enrichment factors flagged Cu, Zn and Cr at traffic- and industry-influenced sites, and PCA separated construction/road dust, vehicular, biomass or food-related and localised industrial factors. Hazard quotients ordered Cr > Pb > Cu > Zn with hazard indices below 1 for both adults and children. The method is the point: leaf-deposited dust is a genuinely zero-power, zero-maintenance passive sampler that resolves metal-enriched microenvironments a sparse reference network cannot. Its limits are equally clear - deposition velocity varies with leaf morphology, species and washoff history, so concentrations are not convertible to airborne mass; the integration time is uncontrolled; and an inhalation hazard quotient computed from deposited dust requires an airborne-concentration assumption that is not observed here.

PAPERS.title: Genomic and Phenotypic Classification of Staphylococcus Species Isolated From Delhi Air.
PAPERS.pm: Culturable bioaerosol sampling (Merck MAS Eco-100), six sites, peak pollution season
PAPERS.n: Outdoor culturable bioaerosol sampling at six Delhi locations in November 2019, the peak pollution month, pre-pandemic. Staphylococcus gallinarum, S. haemolyticus and S. arlettae were recovered and characterised by whole-genome sequencing, phenotypic microarray, antibiotic-resistance profiling and biofilm formation in the presence of black carbon. Comparative genomics found the urease cluster ureABCDEFG in S. arlettae Naraina and S. haemolyticus Yojna Vihar 1, unusual because urease is normally reported negative in both species and may confer a fitness advantage in this niche. The black-carbon biofilm assay is the link to PM and the part most worth following up, but no quantitative result is reported in the abstract. Culture-based sampling recovers a small and biased fraction of the airborne microbiome, six sites and a single month give no seasonal or spatial contrast, and no particle-mass measurements accompany the biological sampling, so the association with the pollution season is contextual rather than measured.

PAPERS.title: Association between polyphenols and inhalation-induced oxidative stress in chronic lung diseases: A systematic review.
PAPERS.pm: Inhalation-induced oxidative stress across in vitro, animal and clinical exposure models
PAPERS.n: Systematic review to January 2026 across PubMed, Cochrane and Web of Science of plant-derived polyphenols in inhalation-associated lung injury, with RoB 2 and SYRCLE risk-of-bias assessment. Preclinical evidence was consistent - attenuated oxidative damage, suppressed inflammatory signalling and enhanced antioxidant defence, largely via Nrf2 activation and NF-kB modulation, with histopathological improvement across several exposure models. Clinical evidence was not: some trials improved oxidative and inflammatory markers or symptom scores, but spirometric effects were inconsistent. That preclinical-to-clinical gap is the familiar signature of antioxidant intervention research and the authors say so. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, so the synthesis is narrative with no pooled estimate. Trials were small and short. Recorded here as the mitigation-side counterpart to the exposure literature, not as evidence that dietary intervention substitutes for reducing the exposure.
